title: Implement policy-decision audit bridge and KMS assertion middleware
author: Priya Rao
release_notes: Adds Policy Decision Audit Bridge and a KMS-backed assertion middleware. No customer-facing API changes. Enables richer, tamper-evident audit records for cross-region RBAC decisions.
body: Summary: This PR introduces a new lightweight 'policy-decision-audit-bridge' service inside the policy stack and a KMS-backed assertion middleware that signs decision digests before they are emitted to the audit pipeline. Motivation: customers and compliance teams have requested cryptographic proof that RBAC decisions were evaluated within the configured jurisdiction and that audit events are tamper-evident during transit. This change provides two capabilities: (1) attach an auditable, content-addressed assertion to every policy decision using a customer/region-aware KMS envelope, and (2) migrate existing audit events into the new bridge so downstream consumers receive a signed assertion + canonicalized event. Key goals: - Ensure assertions are region-anchored (respecting tenant/namespace region pinning) by consulting region hints from the request context. - Keep overhead minimal: signing occurs asynchronously with bounded retries and a local signing cache to avoid blocking critical request paths. - Provide observability and fallbacks: when KMS is unavailable, the bridge emits a signed-placeholder and marks events with 'kms_status: fenced' to be reconciled later. Design: - policy-decision-audit-bridge: a new component receiving canonical policy decisions over an internal pub/sub (existing decisions topic). It canonicalizes the decision payload (deterministic ordering of keys), computes a digest (SHA-256), optionally encrypts the digest with the tenant-scoped CMK, requests a KMS signature/attestation, and forwards combined payload to audit-writer. - kms-assertion-middleware: plumbs into the policy evaluation path and emits a small signed assertion (digest + kms_metadata) for synchronous callers that need proof. Middleware consults namespace-level key-binding policy; if the tenant has 'kms_disabled' flag, it emits 'assertion: unsigned:policy' and a metric. - Signing cache & batching: local LRU cache for recent digests, and batch-sign worker to reduce KMS calls for spikes. - Fallback behavior: on transient KMS failures (<30s), the bridge retries with exponential backoff; for persistent failure, it marks event with 'kms_status: failed' and triggers alert with runbook. Compatibility & rollout: - Backwards compatible: audit-writer can accept both old and new envelope shapes; a compatibility shim added to audit-consumers will read signed_assertion when present. - Rollout plan: feature-flagged (policy.audit.bridge.enabled) rolled out to 5% -> 50% -> 100% tenants. Bridge produces signed assertions in shadow for 2 weeks before enabling enforcement mode. Security considerations: - Tenant-scoped key usage: we enforce that KMS keys are tenant-scoped and validate key location against namespace region. - No plaintext keys stored: only key identifiers and key-policy hashes cached. - Observability: counters for signed/unsigned/placeholder events, KMS latency histograms, and an audit-signing histogram exported to console dashboards. Checklist: - [x] Implement bridge service and middleware - [x] Add unit and integration tests for canonicalization and signing flow - [x] Add metrics and dashboard panels - [x] Feature flag and staged rollout config - [x] Add runbook entry for KMS failure mode - [x] Add Linear ticket references and doc link Documentation: Added docs/ops/policy-decision-audit-bridge.md describing configuration, runbook, and migration notes. Related work: builds on earlier 'region-assertor' work (ENG-6112) and ties into SUP-4127 for customer support triage. Testing: Verified with local KMS emulator and staging tenant with multi-region pin; end-to-end test exercised audit-consumers to validate signature envelope. Impact: Minor additional latency for synchronous middleware path measured at +3ms p50 when cached, +18ms p99 without cache. Cost: Expected KMS request volume reduced by caching and batching; projected increase ~0.6% on average for signing cost for typical workloads.

review_comments: Marco Silva: Please add unit tests for the deterministic canonicalization when map keys include numeric strings. I saw a potential non-determinism in ordering in canonicalizer.go:SerializeMap().
Priya Rao: @Marco added three unit tests that cover numeric key ordering and an explicit sort. SerializeMap now uses stable sort with type-aware comparator.
Elena Dimitrov: We need to ensure the KMS client respects role-bound credentials for operator accounts. Can you scope the signer to use tenant-service-account roles?
Priya Rao: Added KMS role binding lookup and enforced scope; updated docs and added a test to validate role mismatch returns a 403 and placeholder assertion.
Riley Park: Approving after address comments. Small nit: rename 'kms_status' enum to 'kms_assertion_state' to be explicit.
Priya Rao: Renamed field across bridge, middleware, and docs. Adjusted alerts and dashboards accordingly.
conversation_summary: Focused reviews on canonicalization determinism and KMS scoping.
Decided on feature-flagged rollout with shadow signing phase for 2 weeks.
Added runbook and dashboard before enabling enforcement mode.
All reviewers approved; CI green before merge.
